name: Pegasus
introduction: is the winged horse of Greek myth, born from the blood of Medusa. Its body forms the Great Square, a large quadrilateral of four stars that dominates northern autumn skies; one corner, Alpheratz, actually belongs to Andromeda.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Pegasus is the birthplace of exoplanet science. In 1995, Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz discovered a giant planet orbiting 51 Pegasi, a Sun-like star; it was the first planet found around a star like the Sun and earned them the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physics. In 1999, HD 209458, also in Pegasus, became the first star whose planet was seen passing in front of it.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: The Great Square is formed by [Markab](hip:113963), [Scheat](hip:113881), [Algenib](hip:1067) and [Sirrah](hip:677). Scheat is a red giant, and Algenib a hot blue star that pulsates gently.
[Enif](hip:107315), the horse’s nose, is an orange supergiant about 690 light-years away. [Matar](hip:112158), [Homam](hip:112029) and [Biham](hip:109427) mark the neck and legs.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Pegasus contains M15, a dense globular cluster that hosts a planetary nebula. Stephan’s Quintet, a group of interacting galaxies, and the Einstein Cross, where a distant quasar appears as four images bent by a foreground galaxy, also lie here.
